title: Theorem
body_md: If $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting, $\gamma$ is any ordinal, and $\lambda>|T|+|B|+|\gamma|$ is a $k$-ineffable cardinal, then $\lambda\to(\lambda)_{T,\gamma,B}.$
head: environment
name: Hanson

title: Theorem
body_md:
Suppose $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting, $B$ is a parameter set of size at most $\lambda,$ and $\gamma$ is an ordinal. Then,

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $\lambda>|T|+|B|+|\gamma|$ is weakly compact, then $\lambda\to(\lambda)_{T,\gamma,B}$.
        \item If $\lambda\geq|T|+|B|+|\gamma|$, then $\beth_k(\lambda)^+\to(\lambda^+)_{T,\gamma,B}.$
        \item If $\lambda^{|T|}=\lambda$ and $1\leq n < \omega$, then $\beth_{k-1}(\lambda)^+\to(\lambda^+ + (k-1))_{T,n,B}.$
    \end{enumerate}

    Moreover, the hypothesis that $\lambda$ is weakly compact in (1) is optimal.
head: environment

title: Fact
body_md: $T$ is stable if and only if there is a cardinal $\lambda$ such that for any $a$ and $B$, there is a $C\subseteq B$ with $|C|\leq\lambda$ such that $\mathrm{tp}(a/B)$ does not split over $C$.
head: environment
name: Shelah

title: Definition
body_md:
A \emph{$k$-partitioned type} is a type with its variables partitioned into $k$ sets, written $\operatorname{tp}(a_0;\ldots;a_{k-1}/A)$.
For $C\subseteq A$, it \emph{$k$-splits over $C$} if some finite
same-length tuples $b,b'$ from $A$ satisfy
$$
 b\equiv_{Ca_0\cdots\widehat{a_i}\cdots a_{k-1}}b'\quad(i<k),
 \qquad b\not\equiv_{Ca_0\cdots a_{k-1}}b'.
$$
A theory $T$ has \emph{$\lambda$-bounded $k$-splitting} if every such type
with finite blocks has some $C\subseteq A$, $|C|<\lambda$, over which
it does not $k$-split. $T$ has \emph{bounded $k$-splitting} it has $\lambda$-bounded $k$-splitting for some $\lambda$.
head: environment

label: eq:endhom
title: Definition
body_md:
For $1\leq r<\omega$, a sequence $(a_i)_{i<\eta}$ is
\emph{$r$-end-homogeneous over $B$} if
\begin{equation}\label{eq:endhom}
 a_I\equiv_{Ba_{<\alpha}}a_J
 \qquad\bigl(\alpha<\eta,\ I,J\in[\eta\setminus\alpha]^r\bigr).
\end{equation}

$(a_i)_{i<\eta}$ is \emph{end-homogeneous over $B$} if it is
$1$-end-homogeneous over $B$.
head: environment

label: lem:ordinary
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{lem:ordinary}
If $(a_i)_{i<\eta}$ is end-homogeneous over $B$ and every
$\operatorname{tp}(a_i/Ba_{<i})$ does not split over $B$, then the sequence is
indiscernible over $B$.
head: environment

label: thm:basic
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:basic}
If $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting and $\lambda\geq{|T|}+|B|+|\gamma|$, then every sequence of
$\gamma$-tuples of length $\beth_k(\lambda)^+$ has a
$B$-indiscernible subsequence of order type $\lambda^+$.
head: environment

label: fact:smallbase
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fact:smallbase}
If $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting, then every $k$-partitioned type
whose blocks have length $\gamma$ does not $k$-split over some subset
of its parameter domain of size at most ${|T|}+|\gamma|$.
head: environment

label: lem:count
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:count}
Suppose $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting. Fix a parameter set $A$ and
complete types
$$
p_i(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_{k-1})\qquad(i<k)
$$
over $A$, where the variable blocks are finite.
The number of complete types in $x_0,\ldots,x_{k-1}$ over $A$ extending
$\bigcup_{i<k}p_i$ is at most
$$
(|A|+{|T|})^{{|T|}}\cdot 2^{2^{{|T|}}}.
$$
This number is at most $\lambda$ whenever
$|A|\leq\lambda$, $\lambda\geq2^{2^{{|T|}}}$, and
$\lambda^{{|T|}}=\lambda$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Q$ be the set of extensions, and assume $Q\ne\varnothing$.
By Fact~\ref{fact:smallbase}, every $q\in Q$ does not $k$-split over some
$C\subseteq A$ of size at most ${|T|}$. There are at most
$(|A|+{|T|})^{{|T|}}$ possible choices for $C$.

Fix $C$ and a realization $a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}$ of a member of $Q$.
For each $m<\omega$, define an equivalence relation $\sim_C$ on
$A^m$ by setting
$$
\bar b\sim_C\bar b'
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bar b\equiv_{C a_0\cdots\widehat{a_i}\cdots a_{k-1}}\bar b'
\quad(i<k).
$$

There are at most $2^{|T|}$ classes for each $m$.
For each $m$, choose one tuple from each equivalence class in $A^m$,
and let $D_C$ consist of $C$ and all coordinates of the chosen tuples.
Then $|D_C|\leq2^{{|T|}}$.

If $q\in Q$ does not $k$-split over $C$, and $\bar b'$ represents
$\bar b$, non-$k$-splitting gives
$$
\varphi(x_0,\ldots,x_{k-1};\bar b)\in q
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\varphi(x_0,\ldots,x_{k-1};\bar b')\in q.
$$
Thus $q$ is determined by $q\mathbin{\upharpoonright} D_C$. There are at most
$2^{{|T|}+|D_C|}\leq2^{2^{{|T|}}}$ such restrictions, and so summing over $C$
proves the bound.
head: environment

label: lem:ramification
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:ramification}
Let $1\leq r<\omega$ and let
$\lambda\geq{|T|}+|B|+|\gamma|$ be infinite.
Every sequence of $\gamma$-tuples of length $\beth_r(\lambda)^+$
has an $r$-end-homogeneous subsequence over $B$ of order type
$\lambda^++r$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $r=1$, put $\kappa=(2^\lambda)^+$ and write the given sequence as
$(a_i)_{i<\kappa}$. Recursively define families $\mathcal P_\alpha$ of
nonempty subsets of $\kappa$, for $\alpha\leq\lambda^+$.
Let $\mathcal P_0$ partition $\kappa$ by
$i\sim j$ if and only if $a_i\equiv_Ba_j$.
For $X\in\mathcal P_\alpha$, let $D_X$ consist
of $B$ and the coordinates of $a_{\min(X_\xi)}$ for $\xi<\alpha$,
where $X_\xi\in\mathcal P_\xi$ is the unique set containing $X$.
For $\alpha<\lambda^+$, form $\mathcal P_{\alpha+1}$ by partitioning
$X\setminus\{\min(X)\}$, for each $X\in\mathcal P_\alpha$, under
$i\sim_Xj\Longleftrightarrow a_i\equiv_{D_Xa_{\min(X)}}a_j$.
At a nonzero limit $\alpha$, take all nonempty intersections
$\bigcap_{\xi<\alpha}X_\xi$ of decreasing chains with
$X_\xi\in\mathcal P_\xi$.

Inductively, $\mathcal P_\alpha$ partitions the indices not selected as
an earlier $\min(X)$, and $a_i\equiv_{D_X}a_j$ for $i,j\in X$.
For $\alpha<\lambda^+$, $|\mathcal P_\alpha|\leq2^\lambda$: at stage
zero and at successors the relevant parameter sets and the variable
blocks have size at most $\lambda$, and at limits there are at most
$(2^\lambda)^{|\alpha|}=2^\lambda$ chains. Thus at most
$\lambda^+\cdot2^\lambda=2^\lambda$ indices are selected before stage
$\lambda^+$, so $\mathcal P_{\lambda^+}\ne\varnothing$.
Choose $X_{\lambda^+}\in\mathcal P_{\lambda^+}$ and its containing sets
$X_\alpha\in\mathcal P_\alpha$ for $\alpha<\lambda^+$.
Their minima $i_\alpha=\min(X_\alpha)$, $\alpha\leq\lambda^+$, strictly
increase. Since $i_\xi,i_\zeta\in X_\alpha$ for
$\alpha\leq\xi,\zeta\leq\lambda^+$, equality of types over $D_{X_\alpha}$
shows that $(a_{i_\alpha})_{\alpha\leq\lambda^+}$ is end-homogeneous over
$B$.

Now suppose $r > 1$. Put $\mu = \beth_{r-1}(\lambda)$, and put
$\rho = \lambda^+ + (r-1)$. The case $r=1$ gives an end-homogeneous
subsequence $(b_i)_{i<\mu^+} ^\frown (d)$ over $B$.
Since ${|T|} + |Bd| \leq \lambda$, induction over $Bd$ gives a
$(r-1)$-end-homogeneous subsequence $(e_\xi)_{\xi < \rho}$ of
$(b_i)_{i < \mu^+}$. Then the sequence $(e_\xi)_{\xi \leq \rho}$
(setting $e_\rho = d$) is $r$-end-homogeneous over $B$ and has
order type $\lambda^+ + r$.
head: environment

label: lem:tail
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tail}
Suppose $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting and
$\lambda\geq{|T|}+|B|+|\gamma|$ is infinite.
If $\operatorname{cf}(\theta)>\lambda$, every $k$-end-homogeneous sequence of
$\gamma$-tuples of length $\theta$ over $B$ has a
$B$-indiscernible final segment.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(a_i)_{i<\theta}$ be the sequence and put $A_\alpha=Ba_{<\alpha}$.
For each $\alpha<\theta$, define
$$
 p_\alpha(x_0;\ldots;x_{k-1})=\operatorname{tp}(a_I/A_\alpha),
 \qquad I\in[\theta\setminus\alpha]^k.
$$
End-homogeneity makes $p_\alpha$ independent of the choice of $I$
and gives $p_\alpha\subseteq p_\beta$ for $\alpha<\beta$.
Thus $p=\bigcup_{\alpha<\theta}p_\alpha$ is a complete consistent
partitioned type over $Ba_{<\theta}$.
By Fact~\ref{fact:smallbase}, choose $C\subseteq Ba_{<\theta}$ of size
at most ${|T|}+|\gamma|\leq\lambda$ over which $p$ does not
$k$-split. Choose $\beta<\theta$ with $C\subseteq A_\beta$, using
$\operatorname{cf}(\theta)>\lambda$. For every $I\in[\theta\setminus\beta]^k$,
$$
 \operatorname{tp}(a_I/A_{\min I})=p\mathbin{\upharpoonright} A_{\min I}
$$
does not $k$-split over $A_\beta$, which is also true of the realization.

Enumerate the final segment $(a_i)_{\beta\leq i<\theta}$ in order as
$(e_i)_{i<\eta}$, and put $D=A_\beta$. It is
$k$-end-homogeneous over $D$, hence $k$-indiscernible over $D$.
Suppose it is $m$-indiscernible, where $m\geq k$. Write any
increasing $(m+1)$-tuple of its blocks as $uv$, with
$v=(v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1})$ its last $k$ blocks, and put
$u_0=e_0\cdots e_{m-k}$. For each $j<k$, $m$-indiscernibility gives
$$
 u\equiv_{Dv_0\cdots\widehat v_j\cdots v_{k-1}}u_0.
$$
Non-$k$-splitting of the type
of $v$ over its preceding segment gives $uv\equiv_Du_0v$, and
$k$-end-homogeneity gives $u_0v\equiv_De_0\cdots e_m$.
For infinite blocks, each formula uses only finite coordinate subtuples
of $u,u_0$. This proves $(m+1)$-indiscernibility. The final segment is
therefore $D$-indiscernible, hence $B$-indiscernible.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:ramification} with $r=k$ and take the first
$\lambda^+$ tuples of the resulting subsequence. This is a
$k$-end-homogeneous sequence of length $\lambda^+$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:tail} applies since $\operatorname{cf}(\lambda^+)=\lambda^+>\lambda$.
A final segment of $\lambda^+$ has order type $\lambda^+$.
head: environment

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
Suppose $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting, $\lambda^{|T|}=\lambda$, $|B|\leq\lambda$, and $n\geq 1$ is finite. Then every sequence of $n$-tuples of length $\beth_{k-1}(\lambda)^+$ has a $B$-indiscernible subsequence of length $\lambda^+ + (k-1).$
head: environment

label: lem:fodor
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:fodor}
Suppose $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting,
$\lambda\geq{|T|}$,  $\lambda^{|T|}=\lambda$, and $|B|\leq\lambda$.
Assume that every family of types as in Lemma~\ref{lem:count} over any set of
size at most $\lambda$ has at most $\lambda$ common complete extensions.
Then every sequence of $n$-tuples of length $\lambda^+$ that is
$(k-1)$-end-homogeneous over $B$ has a
$B$-indiscernible subsequence of order type $\lambda^+$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(a_i)_{i<\theta}$ be the given sequence, where $\theta=\lambda^+$.
Put $A_\alpha=B\cup a_{<\alpha}$ and $A=B\cup a_{<\theta}$.
Adjoin tuples $c_1,\ldots,c_{k-1}$ in an elementary
extension so that $(a_i)_{i<\theta}\mathbin{{}^\frown}(c_1,\ldots,c_{k-1})$
is still $(k-1)$-end-homogeneous over $B$.
To do this, realize the increasing union
$$
\bigcup_{\alpha<\theta}\operatorname{tp}(a_I/A_\alpha),
\qquad I\in[\theta\setminus\alpha]^{k-1}.
$$

Put $c=c_1\cdots c_{k-1}$.
Then we have, for every $\alpha<\theta$ and $1\leq j<k$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:restrictions}
 a_\alpha c_1\cdots\widehat{c_j}\cdots c_{k-1}
 \equiv_{A_\alpha}c_1\cdots c_{k-1}.
\end{equation}

By Fact~\ref{fact:smallbase}, choose $C_\alpha\subseteq A_\alpha$,
$|C_\alpha|\leq{|T|}$, such that
$\operatorname{tp}(a_\alpha;c_1;\ldots;c_{k-1}/A_\alpha)$ does not $k$-split over
$C_\alpha$. We claim that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ordinary}
 \operatorname{tp}(a_\alpha/A_\alpha c)\text{ does not split over }C_\alpha c.
\end{equation}
Indeed, if $\bar b,\bar b'\in A_\alpha^{<\omega}$ satisfy
$\bar b\equiv_{C_\alpha c}\bar b'$, then \eqref{eq:restrictions} transfers
this equality to the parameters obtained by omitting any one block from
$a_\alpha,c_1,\ldots,c_{k-1}$. Non-$k$-splitting therefore gives
$\bar b\equiv_{C_\alpha a_\alpha c}\bar b'$.
For tuples from $A_\alpha c$, equality over $C_\alpha c$ forces
coordinates belonging to $c$ to match. Delete those coordinates,
apply the preceding argument, and reinsert them.

On the stationary set
$\{\alpha<\theta:\operatorname{cf}(\alpha)={|T|}^+\}$, the coordinates of
$C_\alpha\setminus B$ occur below some index $\beta_\alpha<\alpha$.
Here ${|T|}^+<\theta$, since $2^{{|T|}}\leq\lambda^{{|T|}}=\lambda$.
Fodor's lemma gives a stationary set on which $\beta_\alpha$ is constant,
say with value $\beta$. Since $|A_\beta|\leq\lambda$ and
$\lambda^{{|T|}}=\lambda$, we may thin further to a stationary set
$S$ on which $C_\alpha$ is fixed, say with value $C$.

For each $m<\omega$, let $R_m\subseteq A^m$ contain exactly one
representative of each equivalence class for the equivalence relation
defined by letting
$\bar b\sim_m\bar b'\Longleftrightarrow\bar b\equiv_{Cc}\bar b'$.
Let $D$ consist of $C$ and all coordinates of tuples in
$\bigcup_{m<\omega}R_m$. Since $|Cc|\leq{|T|}$, we have
$|R_m|\leq2^{{|T|}}$ and hence $|D|\leq2^{{|T|}}\leq\lambda$.
Choose $\delta<\theta$ with $D\subseteq A_\delta$, and discard indices
at most $\delta$ from $S$.
For $\alpha\in S$, put
$q_\alpha=\operatorname{tp}(a_\alpha,c_1,\ldots,c_{k-1}/A_\delta)$.
Let $p_i(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_{k-1})$ be
$\operatorname{tp}(c/A_\delta)$ with its variable blocks renamed in order $(i<k)$.
By \eqref{eq:restrictions}, $q_\alpha\supseteq\bigcup_{i<k}p_i$.
The hypothesis on common complete extensions, applied to these types
over $A_\delta$, where $|A_\delta|\leq\lambda$, gives at most
$\lambda$ possible $q_\alpha$. Thin to a stationary $S'\subseteq S$
on which they agree.
Thus the $a_\alpha$, $\alpha\in S'$, have the same type over
$A_\delta c$.

If $\alpha<\alpha'$ belong to $S'$ and $\bar b\in A_\alpha^m$,
choose $\bar d\in R_m\subseteq D^m$ with
$\bar b\equiv_{Cc}\bar d$. Applying \eqref{eq:ordinary} at both indices
gives, for every formula $\varphi$,
$$
\varphi(a_\alpha;\bar b,c)
\ \iff\ \varphi(a_\alpha;\bar d,c)
\ \iff\ \varphi(a_{\alpha'};\bar d,c)
\ \iff\ \varphi(a_{\alpha'};\bar b,c).
$$
Consequently $a_\alpha\equiv_{A_\alpha c}a_{\alpha'}$.
The sequence $(a_\alpha)_{\alpha\in S'}$ is end-homogeneous over
$A_\delta c$. By \eqref{eq:ordinary}, restriction and enlargement of the
base show that each successive type does not split over $A_\delta c$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:ordinary} therefore gives indiscernibility over
$A_\delta c$, hence over $B$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:ramification}, the given sequence
$(a_i)_{i<\beth_{k-1}(\lambda)^+}$ has a $(k-1)$-end-homogeneous
subsequence $(b_j)_{j<\lambda^++(k-1)}$ over $B$, where
$b_j=a_{\xi_j}$ and the indices $\xi_j$ are strictly increasing.
Lemma~\ref{lem:count} shows that the hypothesis of
Lemma~\ref{lem:fodor} is satisfied, so we may apply it  to the first
$\lambda^+$ tuples gives a $B$-indiscernible subsequence indexed by a
cofinal $Y\subseteq\lambda^+$ of order type $\lambda^+$,
say $(c_i)_{i<\lambda^+}$. Then the sequence
$(c_i)_{i<\lambda^+}\;^\frown
(b_{\lambda^+},\ldots,b_{\lambda^++k-2})$
is a $B$-indiscernible sequence.
head: environment

label: cor:larger
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:larger}
Suppose $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting and
$\mu\geq 2^{{|T|}}$. For every positive finite $n$,
$$
\beth_k(\mu)^+\longrightarrow
\bigl((2^\mu)^++(k-1)\bigr)_{T,n}.
$$
The same conclusion holds over any parameter set $B$ with $|B|\leq\mu$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $\lambda=2^\mu$. Then $\lambda\geq2^{2^{|T|}}$,
$\lambda^{|T|}=\lambda$, and
$\beth_{k-1}(\lambda)=\beth_k(\mu)$. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
head: environment

label: thm:weak
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:weak}
Suppose $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting, where $1\leq k<\omega$, and
$\kappa>{|T|}+|B|+|\gamma|$ is weakly compact.
Every sequence of $\gamma$-tuples of length $\kappa$ has a
$B$-indiscernible subsequence of order type $\kappa$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose an infinite ${|T|}+|B|+|\gamma|\leq\lambda<\kappa$.
We first prove, by induction on $r\geq1$, that every sequence of
$\gamma$-tuples of length $\kappa$ has an $r$-end-homogeneous
subsequence of order type $\kappa$.

For $r=1$, carry out the partition construction in
Lemma~\ref{lem:ramification} on the given index set $\kappa$, at every
stage $\alpha<\kappa$. Its levels satisfy
$$
 |\mathcal P_\alpha|\leq2^{\lambda+|\alpha|}<\kappa.
$$
The strict inequality uses the strong inaccessibility of $\kappa$.
Indeed, the right-hand side bounds the number of types over the parameters
on a branch of length $\alpha$, and at a limit it also bounds the number
of preceding chains. Every $\mathcal P_\alpha$ is nonempty by the
regularity of $\kappa$.
Order the nodes $(\alpha,X)$, $X\in\mathcal P_\alpha$, by
$$
 (\alpha,X)<(\beta,Y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \alpha<\beta\text{ and }Y\subseteq X.
$$
Each node has exactly one predecessor at every previous level.
After adjoining a root, this is a tree to which the tree property
applies. The downward closure of a cofinal branch gives classes
$X_\alpha\in\mathcal P_\alpha$ for all $\alpha<\kappa$.
Their minima strictly increase and index an end-homogeneous
subsequence of length $\kappa$, by the same type equalities as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:ramification}.

For $r>1$, first obtain an end-homogeneous subsequence
$(b_i)_{i<\kappa}$. In an elementary extension choose a
$\gamma$-tuple $d$ realizing
$$
 \bigcup_{\alpha<\kappa}\operatorname{tp}(b_i/Bb_{<\alpha}),
 \qquad \alpha\leq i<\kappa.
$$
The types in this union are well-defined and increasing, so the union
is consistent and complete. Consequently
$(b_i)_{i<\kappa}\mathbin{{}^\frown}(d)$ is end-homogeneous over $B$.
Apply induction over $Bd$ to $(b_i)_{i<\kappa}$.
Replacing the last block in each compared $r$-tuple by $d$, exactly
as in Lemma~\ref{lem:ramification}, shows that the selected
$(r-1)$-end-homogeneous sequence over $Bd$ is
$r$-end-homogeneous over $B$.

Take $r=k$. Lemma~\ref{lem:tail} applies at $\theta=\kappa$, since
$\operatorname{cf}(\kappa)=\kappa>\lambda$. Its indiscernible final segment has order
type $\kappa$.
head: environment

label: fact:chain
title: Fact
head: environment

label: fact:totality
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fact:totality}
A $B$-indiscernible sequence $(a_i)_{i<\omega}$ is total bu-Morley
over $B$ if and only if there are infinite sequences $I,J$ such that
$I+J\equiv_B^{\mathrm{EM}}(a_i)_{i<\omega}$ and $I\mathrel{\raise0.2ex\hbox{\ooalign{\hidewidth$\vert$\hidewidth\cr\raise-0.9ex\hbox{$\smile$}}}}^{\mathrm{bu}}_BJ$.
head: environment

label: lem:butree
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:butree}
For every infinite cardinal $\mu$, parameter set $B$, and set-sized
tuple $a$, there are tuples $(d_\xi)_{\xi<\mu}$, with
$d_\xi\equiv_Ba$, and, for each $\xi<\mu$, a bu-Morley sequence
$(c_i^\xi)_{i<\omega}$ over $B$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:treeinput}
 d_{<\xi}\subseteq\operatorname{rng}(c_0^\xi),
 \qquad
 (c_i^\xi)_{i<\omega}\text{ is indiscernible over }Bd_{>\xi}.
\end{equation}
Here $d_{<\xi}$ and $d_{>\xi}$ denote the sets of coordinates of the
earlier and later tuples, respectively.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal T_\mu$ be the tree of finitely supported functions
$f:[\beta,\mu)\to\omega$, where $\beta<\mu$ is zero or a successor
ordinal, ordered by extension. The tree construction in \cite{HansonBU} gives
an $s$-indiscernible, bu-spread-out family
$(t_f)_{f\in\mathcal T_\mu}$ over $B$, with $t_f\equiv_Ba$ for every
$f$.

For each $\xi<\mu$, let $f_\xi$ be identically zero on $[\xi+2,\mu)$,
and put $d_\xi=t_{f_\xi}$. For $i<\omega$, set
$g_i^\xi=f_\xi\cup\{(\xi+1,i)\}$ and let $c_i^\xi$ be the
concatenation of the tuples $t_g$ for $g\in\mathcal T_\mu$ with
$g\supseteq g_i^\xi$.
Use enumerations matched by the map that changes only the value at
$\xi+1$. The domains of $f_\xi$ and $g_i^\xi$ start at successor
ordinals, so both are nodes of $\mathcal T_\mu$.
Then $(c_i^\xi)_{i<\omega}$ is bu-Morley over $B$.

If $\eta<\xi$, then $f_\eta\supseteq g_0^\xi$, so every coordinate of
$d_\eta$ occurs in $c_0^\xi$. If $\eta>\xi$, then $f_\eta$ is a restriction
of all the subtrees rooted at $g_i^\xi$. The $s$-indiscernibility
then$(c_i^\xi)_{i<\omega}$ indiscernible over $Bd_{>\xi}$.
This also holds for the whole subtree tuples, since each formula uses
only finitely many coordinates.
head: environment

label: thm:totalbu
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:totalbu}
Suppose $T$ has bounded $k$-splitting for some $1\leq k<\omega$.
For every parameter set $B$ and every possibly infinite tuple $a$,
there is a total bu-Morley sequence $(a_i)_{i<\omega}$ over $B$
with $a_0=a$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose an infinite $\lambda\geq{|T|}+|B|+|a|$ and put
$\mu=\beth_k(\lambda)^+$. Theorem~\ref{thm:basic} gives extraction of
order type $\lambda^+$, hence of order type $\omega+\omega$, over
$B$ for tuples of length $|a|$.

Choose the tuples supplied by Lemma~\ref{lem:butree} and extract a
$B$-indiscernible subsequence $(d_{\xi_j})_{j<\omega+\omega}$, where
the $\xi_j$ strictly increase. Put
$$
 I=(d_{\xi_j})_{j<\omega},\qquad
 \rho=\xi_\omega,\qquad
 J=(d_{\xi_{\omega+1+j}})_{j<\omega}.
$$
Then $I+J$ is $B$-indiscernible. Every coordinate of $I$ occurs
in $c_0^\rho$, and $(c_i^\rho)_{i<\omega}$ is indiscernible over
$BJ$. Fact~\ref{fact:chain}, applied with one tuple enumerating the
whole of $J$, gives $c_0^\rho\mathrel{\raise0.2ex\hbox{\ooalign{\hidewidth$\vert$\hidewidth\cr\raise-0.9ex\hbox{$\smile$}}}}^{\mathrm{bu}}_BJ$.
Monotonicity gives $I\mathrel{\raise0.2ex\hbox{\ooalign{\hidewidth$\vert$\hidewidth\cr\raise-0.9ex\hbox{$\smile$}}}}^{\mathrm{bu}}_BJ$, and Fact~\ref{fact:totality}
shows that $I$ is total bu-Morley over $B$.
Finally, $d_{\xi_0}\equiv_Ba$: an automorphism fixing $B$ sends
$d_{\xi_0}$ to $a$ and sends $I$ to the required sequence.
head: environment
